# Friday small groups {.unnumbered}

[One hour every Friday, required, in one of three time slots · practise talking about AI out loud]{.subtitle .lead}

Being able to talk about AI with an attending, a colleague, a patient, or an
interviewer is a skill, and it gets better with practice, not reading. Friday
is where you practise.

## How the hour runs

| Minutes | What |
|---|---|
| 0 to 15 | Round the group: one thing AI helped you learn this week, and one thing you caught it getting wrong. From your [learning journal](learning-journal.qmd). |
| 15 to 45 | Breakout rooms of four or five, the same people each week. Two scenario cards, below. |
| 45 to 60 | Back together: what was hard to say, and what worked. |

: The Friday hour. {#tbl-friday}

**How to use a card.** One person plays the role on the card, one answers, and
the others watch. Three minutes, then two minutes of feedback: what landed,
what was vague, what was more certain than the evidence allows. Swap roles and
run it again. There is no right script. The goal is to sound like yourself:
informed, honest about what you do not know, and not defensive.

## The cards

### Week 1 (October 16): introductions

**The interview question.** *Play: a residency interviewer.* "So, what do you
think about AI in medicine?" Then one follow-up: "Do you use it yourself?"

**The worried classmate.** *Play: a classmate who has never used a chatbot.* "I
keep hearing it makes things up. Why would I trust it with anything?"

### Week 2 (October 23)

**The skeptical attending.** *Play: an attending.* "I saw you had ChatGPT open.
We don't do that on my service. Convince me it's not a shortcut."

**The fair score.** *Play: a resident.* "This risk score doesn't use race, so it
can't be biased." The answerer explains how a score can be unfair without
using race at all. [The bias chapter](../chapters/core-bias-equity.qmd) has the
examples.

**The co-intern who pasted it in.** *Play: a co-intern.* "I put the discharge
summary into ChatGPT on my phone to clean it up. I took the name out. That's
fine, right?" See [the patient information
page](patient-information.qmd).

### Week 3 (October 30)

**The scribe question.** *Play: a patient.* "Is that phone listening to us? Who
hears this?" [Talking to patients about
AI](../chapters/core-patient-communication.qmd) covers this conversation.

**The caregiver who came prepared.** *Play: a parent or adult child.* "I talked
it through with ChatGPT last night. It said we should get an MRI and see a
specialist, and I want both today."

**The patient who talks to a bot instead.** *Play: a patient.* "Honestly, I talk
to an AI app about my anxiety more than I talk to anyone. It helps. Is that
bad?"

### Week 4 (November 6): what you will keep

The week 4 hour is for your five-minute presentations from the
[learning journal](learning-journal.qmd). If there is time, one last card:

**The trust question.** *Play: a friend.* "I asked a chatbot who to vote for and
it gave me a really reasonable answer. Why not just go with it?" Talk about
where an answer comes from, and who decides what a chatbot says.

**The incoming intern.** *Play: a nervous new intern next July.* "Should I be
using this stuff? Where do I start?"
